name: Analytical Figure Classification
shortcutSummary: Figures are pre-sorted into two groups based on a hidden rule. Identify the rule by comparing the two groups, then classify the question figure into the correct group.
conceptExplanation: Analytical Figure Classification questions show figures divided into two groups (Set 1 and Set 2) and ask you to determine which set a new figure belongs to. You must identify the classification rule.

subtopics.name: Analytical Figure Classification — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation: Analytical Figure Classification questions show figures divided into two groups (Set 1 and Set 2) and ask you to determine which set a new figure belongs to. You must identify the classification rule.
shortcuts: Compare Sets: List properties of each set and find what differentiates them.
Common Properties: Check for: number of elements, open/closed shapes, straight/curved lines, shading, symmetry.
Process of Elimination: If the question figure has a property unique to Set 1, it belongs to Set 1.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Which of the following figures belongs to the class where the outer polygon has exactly ONE more side than the inner polygon?
options: A regular pentagon enclosing a square (5 sides outer, 4 sides inner)
A square enclosing a regular pentagon (4 sides outer, 5 sides inner)
A regular hexagon enclosing a triangle (6 sides outer, 3 sides inner)
A regular pentagon enclosing an equilateral triangle (5 sides outer, 3 sides inner)
practiceQuestions.hint: Count outer sides versus inner sides (n and n - 1).
practiceQuestions.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 sides and an enclosed square has 4 sides; the difference is exactly 5 - 4 = 1 side. This satisfies the classification criterion.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Understand the analytical classification rule stated in the prompt.
Step 2: Evaluate the geometric properties (side counts, partition counts, area ratios) of each option.
Step 3: The uniquely matching figure is A regular pentagon enclosing a square (5 sides outer, 4 sides inner).

practiceQuestions.questionText: Which figure has exactly 25% (one quarter) of its total area shaded?
options: A circle divided into four quadrants with two quadrants shaded (50%)
An equilateral triangle with three smaller congruent triangles inside and one shaded (33%)
A circle divided into four equal quadrants with exactly one quadrant shaded black
A regular hexagon with three of its six triangular sectors shaded (50%)
practiceQuestions.hint: One part out of four equal parts equals 25%.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Dividing a circle into 4 equal 90-degree quadrant sectors and shading one sector yields an exact 1/4 = 25% shaded area fraction.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Understand the analytical classification rule stated in the prompt.
Step 2: Evaluate the geometric properties (side counts, partition counts, area ratios) of each option.
Step 3: The uniquely matching figure is A circle divided into four equal quadrants with exactly one quadrant shaded black.

practiceQuestions.questionText: Identify the figure which is divided into exactly eight congruent parts by its internal diagonals and axes:

A circle divided into ten congruent sectors

practiceQuestions.questionText: In which figure do three identical circles intersect such that each circle passes through the centers of the other two?
options: Two intersecting circles touching a third tangential circle
Three concentric circles with equal radial spacing
Symmetrical Venn trefoil with a central Reuleaux-like triangular overlap
Three mutually exclusive disjoint circles
practiceQuestions.hint: Recall the classical geometry of three mutually center-intersecting circles.
practiceQuestions.explanation: When three congruent circles pass through each other's centers, they form a classic trefoil symmetry with 7 bounded internal regions.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Understand the analytical classification rule stated in the prompt.
Step 2: Evaluate the geometric properties (side counts, partition counts, area ratios) of each option.
Step 3: The uniquely matching figure is Symmetrical Venn trefoil with a central Reuleaux-like triangular overlap.
